message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $362 and am on ATLANTIC_AVENUE. My Orange monopoly has four houses each, and my Pink monopoly has two houses each. I hold one GOOJF card. Claude has $345 and owns red properties at three to four houses. He also holds mortgaged Pacific and Penn RR. Player three is bankrupt.

Gemini has $126 and owns yellows with one to two houses. The bank has no houses left but twelve hotels. I will keep the housing lock and avoid hotels. I can trade with Claude or Gemini, unmortgage my four properties, or build hotels on my Orange monopoly.

I am calculating hotel costs. Orange properties cost $100 per house, so a hotel there costs $100 and returns four houses to the bank.

Building a hotel on an orange property would return four houses to the bank. Claude could then buy two houses for $300 and reach four houses on Kentucky and Indiana. He would still have two houses left in the bank. This makes hotels a poor choice.

Claude could build a hotel on Illinois for $150. That would return four houses to the bank and raise rent to $1100.

Standard Monopoly rent values are being verified. Orange hotels pay $950 to $1000, while red hotels pay $1050. Claude could build two houses on Kentucky and Indiana for $300 to reach four houses each.

Standard Monopoly rent values are now confirmed. Red four-house rents are $875 each, and Illinois hotel rent is $1100. Orange four-house rents are $750 each, and orange hotels pay $950 to $1000.

Hoteling is confirmed as a poor choice. Claude could build a hotel on Illinois for $150 and still afford another house on Kentucky for $150, leaving him with four houses on three properties. Unmortgage costs are being checked next.

Unmortgaging would cost $264 and yield only small rents. My $362 cash buffer is safer than paying Claude's red four-house rents. Selling houses is also ruled out because the bank has no houses left to buy. I am now considering trade options.

Gemini is the weaker opponent. He has only $126 cash and low yellow houses. If he lands on my orange properties at four houses, he could go bankrupt or be forced to sell everything. I am calculating his liquidation value.

Gemini's liquidation value is roughly $456. He cannot pay my orange four-house rents of $750 or $800 even with all cash and houses sold. He would go bankrupt to me. I am now checking pink two-house rent values.

Pink two-house rent is $150 to $180. Gemini can pay this with his $126 cash, but he would need to sell a house for $75. I am now deciding which optional actions to take before ending my turn.

I am weighing trade offers to acquire Boardwalk or Park Place, though neither would complete a dark blue monopoly alone. I am also considering mortgaged railroads from the other players.

Railroad trades are not worth the cost. Both opponents want me bankrupt because my orange properties are lethal. Any trade that gives them houses or cash would let them build and strengthen themselves. I will end my turn without trading.

I am mapping the next roll options from Atlantic Avenue. Ventnor and Marvin Gardens are yellow properties with one and two houses respectively, while Water Works, Pacific, Pennsylvania Ave, and Park Place are mortgaged and pay no rent. North Carolina is unowned and may require a purchase. I am now calculating the yellow rent values.

Standard yellow rent values are confirmed. Ventnor at one house pays $110 and Marvin Gardens at two houses pays $360. Both are affordable with my current cash. I will not buy North Carolina Avenue now because it is unowned and would leave me short of cash.

I am weighing whether to use my GOOJF card to enter Jail on a roll of five, which would temporarily shield me from rent. I also considered trading my mortgaged light blue properties for Gemini's Oriental and Mediterranean, but that would not complete a set.

I will not trade my mortgaged light blue properties to Gemini. That would complete his light blue or brown monopolies, which would strengthen him rather than weaken him. I also considered buying Boardwalk from Claude, but he would demand a large price for the missing dark blue piece.

I will end my turn without trading. I am keeping my public message brief and consistent with previous terse updates.

I rejected the idea of selling a house for cash. I also considered trading my GOOJF card for money, but the card is too valuable as a jail shelter against Claude's red four-house rents.

Claude is on Kentucky. He can land on my orange properties at one house, or on my yellow properties at two houses. He has $345 cash and may need to sell a house to pay rent.

Claude cannot land on my orange or pink properties from Kentucky this turn. He is safe from rent and cannot build. Gemini can reach Marvin Gardens at two houses, but he cannot afford to buy North Carolina Avenue with only $126.
